also: say whatever comes into one’s head
off the top of one’s head

terms.grammar: relative clause with in buccam (bucca, the cheek)
terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Cic. in epistulīs; Mart.
evidence: Cic. Att. 12.1.2: garrīmus quicquid in buccam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally “into the cheek”: Lewis & Short, “a colloq. phrase, to speak (write) whatever comes uppermost”. For an idea that occurs to one, in mentem venit (see idea).

sources: Lewis & Short: bucca
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
